notes:
Typing a piston number that is already used in the same piece now warns you.

**Set a piston to a number another piston in this piece already has, and you get a warning** saying which page it is on, with Continue or Cancel. Until now that never warned at all — the check only ever looked at other pieces, and it skipped pistons with no memory level entirely, so on an organ without memory levels no number ever warned.

It only warns when you type the number yourself. Placing pistons the normal way stays quiet: a number already used is skipped automatically, which is how a run carries on across both tablets without a prompt every time.

Other pieces are unchanged. A piston with no memory level still does not warn about the same number in another piece, because those are the temporary pieces you re-register each week.
